Title: The Real Reason Behind That Sulfur Smell in Your Throat

Description:
Tonsil stones (tonsilloliths) form when food debris, dead cells, and bacteria get trapped in the crypts on your tonsils and calcify into a hard lump. Even a grain-sized stone can smell surprisingly strong — bad breath is the most common symptom, and larger stones can cause a scratchy throat or referred ear pain.

Frequent tonsillitis widens the crypts over time, dehydration and mouth breathing slow down saliva's natural cleansing, and leftover food debris from poor oral hygiene gives them more to form from. Gargling with warm salt water, staying hydrated, and keeping up with brushing and flossing all help keep them from coming back.

Don't dig them out with your finger or a cotton swab — that can scrape the tonsil tissue. If they keep recurring, an ENT doctor can offer in-office removal or a procedure called cryptolysis.
